text: "I was there" - Reliving history is a potential that gaming should embrace (image showing the execution of Louis XVI, AC Unity) I will preface this by stating, I am not a French, and this is not a critique of the French politics or social issues, which are entirely the country's own business. This past weekend, news of violent riots and looting across France shocked the world. As the proud Republic treads a tenuous ground, images of chaos and disorder reminded me of the French Revolution. It's a pivotal moment in history that many of us have witnessed, in a sense, through Assassin's Creed Unity. AC the franchise is much maligned today, so it's easy to forget how successful they have been in depicting history as entertainment. From the beheading of Louis XVI to the Boston Tea Party, we had a first person view on some of the most critical events in the history of the Western world. Not only is that rare in gaming - even AC itself has somewhat moved away from that approach. I made this post to argue that, there is a place in gaming to record and reenact history, and to position itself as a powerful medium to engage the public in understanding the experience and lessons of the past. I don't mean just starting a new Civ campaign or BF match. I mean truly living and witnessing the movement, the people, the ideas and the outcomes as a protagonist, Very few games embrace that potential, which imo can help foster stronger interest in a subject matter that, well, most of us slept through in school 🤣 And that form of preservation is important because the digital/AI era will distort our social memories and national identities in precedented ways. Having well researched and narrated history in the most popular form of entertainment in the world offers at least one more solution to that problem. It is a luxury, but also a necessity imo. Anyway just some quick thoughts. Don't let them bother you if it's not your cup of tea lol. Have a good one - and my best wishes to the people of France.

text: OPINION: Developers should downgrade graphics back to 2015 - 2018. The hyperfixation in game ever more realistic graphics is increasing development costs over the skies, when there's not even a significant gain in game quality at all. More than that, we've actually been seeing huge losses in game density and performance. There's also something weird about ultra realistic games, when they lose that "3D modelled" appearance and just become close to photorrealism. It feels off. 2015 - 2018 IMO was the peak of graphics, with different arts too: Batman Arkham Knight, The Witcher 3, Red Dead Redemption 2 and Metal Gear Solid V. All of them have totally different art styles, and yet they're all realistic and beautiful enough, without compromising the feeling of it still being a game. I see no problem in backtracking what was good and using some of these resources to add depth/content to games. It's just my opinion though, no need to get all sensible about it. I still like realistic graphics in some games, but it's becoming quite difficult to find companies that manage to create both realism (to modern standards) and quality in AAA games.

text: Do you see Metacritic and Opencritic respective top 1 games getting dethroned? Metacritic and Gamerankings got created around the same time in 1999...and since it's inception, a single game was always top 1 in Metacritic, Ocarina of Time, which to this day, keeps that spot...almost 20 years later Gamerankings used to be like that too, but a game actually got to dethrone Ocarina of Time for top 1, being Mario Galaxy in 2007 (almost 10 years after Ocarina of Time), and stayed top 1 until Gamerankings closure in 2019 (merging with Metacritic), keeping the record for over 10 years and now it's part of the legacy of it as well. A new aggregation site was created in 2015 though, being Opencritic, more focused on modern games. For once, Nintendo wasn't at the top, as GTA 4 was found rulling as top 1...but that changed a measly two years later, cause Breath of the Wild claimed top 1...then Mario Odyssey, keeping it nowdays almost 10 years later. text: Why you shouldn't buy into the hype surrounding Squadron42. I am not falling into the Squadron42 hype. Its being hyped quite a bit. My YouTube feed - and I assume - the YouTube feeds of anyone that follows Star Citizen, is filled with positive content surrounding the title. But I'm not falling into it... Because I remember I remember I remember when SQ42 was initially slated to release in 2014, and it was then pushed back, not for a year, or two years, or even three years, but 12 fucking years. 12... fucking... years... I remember that, I know that most have forgotten, but I have not. I remember the tales of Server Meshing going into Star Citizen in 2017. Server Meshing didn't go in until like 2023. That's a 7 year gap. I remember the "Year of Playability" for Star Citizen. The year that was supposted to take that game, and transform it from buggy wreck into a polished and solid game that you could play. That year has passed, and I've played Star Citizen recently, and its still a buggy wreck. CIG lies And they're extravagant lies. The game is still an alpha after 14 years they say. You shouldn't expect better they say. Its not too long they say, its just like GTA6 (this is wrong, Rockstar released RDR2 - arguably the best game ever made - in 2018, GTA6 comes only 8 years after their last masterpiece mega-hit, claiming that development took 14 years is what happens when you count from GTA5's release, and include every moment anyone even thought about GTA6 - even when they were hard at work on RDR2). 14 years is normal for a AAA game they say - also a lie. I might be wrong Its possible, maybe SQ42 will indeed release in 2027 (I doubt it) and maybe it will really be this masterpiece AAA level game, but I doubt it. I really doubt it. I doubt it because where there's smoke, there's usually fire. We have every reason to believe that CIG is mostly incapable of delivering a compelling game experience. They've failed with Star Citizen - at least so far - and the 12 year gap with regard to SQ42 tells us that they're full of shit. No game is ready and then gets a 12 year delay. If it was really ready, it wouldn't have gotten a 12 year delay. The one thing CIG does well, is control the conversation Here on reddit, criticize CIG, and eventually mods will come after you. I've been banned from several Star Citizen reddits for being critical of the game. I was once banned from an SC reddit for merely pointing out that Star CItizen has been in development for 14 years - as that's apparently not something you're allowed to bring up in Star Citizen circles. I do not know for sure that CIG controls most of the SC subs here on reddit, but I suspect they do. And of course they also controlled the press surrounding their Squadron42 event. Only the whitest of white knight YouTube content creators were allowed to attend. No real press. Its hard to prove a negative, but as far as I can tell, no one from Gamespot or IGN was invited. This was a giveaway to biased CIG influencers, who are out there doing CIG a solid day in day out by talking about amazing upcoming features and not talking about delays, bugs, and the failure of CIG to deliver. I think they've controlled the conversation surrounding SQ42. Time will tell, but I'm not buying the hype. EDIT: Look at the CIG bots go.
